correctness.summary: The right-angled-hexagon cosine law gives the half-angle identity for each seam; multiplying the three formulas yields the closed mass expression. A product-to-sum identity gives the symmetric denominator form. Strict convexity of the translated cosh sum proves Schur-concavity, and the equal-cuff maximum, degenerate infimum, and sharp one-half bound follow algebraically. The numerical artifact is only a cross-check, not the proof.

final_claim: For a compact hyperbolic pair of pants, the total Basmajian contribution of the three inter-cuff seams has the stated closed formula, is strictly Schur-concave in the cuff lengths at fixed total boundary, has the stated exact range with equal-cuff maximizer, and is always less than half the total boundary with sharp constant.

residual_risks: Because the derivation uses classical hyperbolic trigonometry, equivalent older orthospectral folklore under different notation remains a real residual risk.
originality.summary: The Basmajian identity and right-angled-hexagon trigonometry are classical and are not claimed as new. Full/open inspections of the Luo–Tan pants-measure literature and the prime-orthogeodesic identity paper concern different summands or broader identity families; no fixed-total strict majorization theorem, exact range, or sharp one-half bound for precisely the three inter-cuff Basmajian seam terms was located.

value.summary: The three seams are canonical geometric objects and their Basmajian contribution is a natural part of the boundary-length identity. The theorem gives a complete fixed-total extremal law and sharp asymptotic share, a motivated structural statement rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
